clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. She exhibited a cheerful and cooperative demeanor initially, but her attention span was noted as moderately limited, with frequent occurrences of distractibility. Muscle tone was within normal limits, and range of motion was appropriate for her age. Sabrina showed patterns of consistent engagement when activities were intrinsically motivating but displayed diminished participation during structured tasks, needing maximal verbal and visual cues. Fine motor skills revealed challenges, with visual-motor integration tasks requiring direct hand-over-hand assistance. The presence of these challenges necessitated modifications to testing procedures to support optimal engagement. Behavioral observations indicated that structured task settings occasionally heightened task avoidance responses, influencing the standardized testing processes and affecting the validity of some measures.
